findings.element: Key field input in the matching-rule configurator (required once a metadata source is chosen)
findings.finding: The key field's required status is only revealed by an error summary after Update is pressed — nothing marks it as required while the user is filling out the form.
findings.user_impact: A user can pick a metadata source, believe the rule is complete, and press Update, only then discovering a field they never saw flagged as mandatory — the exact abandonment risk a multi-field setup needs to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the key field as required inline (asterisk or helper text) as soon as a metadata source is selected, before the user reaches Update.

evidence.action: Opened the matching configurator, selected a metadata source, left the key field empty, then pressed Update.
evidence.observed: The overlay stayed open and a summary message appeared listing the missing key — the requirement was not indicated anywhere before that point.

gaps: Close without saving: not exercised in this slice — unknown whether it discards silently or shows a confirmation, so consistency with the X-close discard prompt can't be verified.

Update (successful commit): not exercised in this slice — unknown whether any persistent saved-state confirmation appears afterward, which bears directly on the known pattern of users re-opening the panel to check whether a change saved.

Escape key: the recorded test doesn't state whether unsaved changes were present when Escape closed the overlay, so it's unknown whether Escape bypasses the discard-confirmation shown for the X-close button.

Toggle-style controls inside the configurator: the state map doesn't record whether flipping a setting produces any visible on-screen effect, so the 'toggle then toggle back' friction pattern can't be checked.
